summary.text: Jonathan Jackson is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for Illinois' 1st District, in office since January 2023. The son of civil rights leader Rev. Jesse Jackson, he worked as a business owner, finance instructor and national spokesman for the Rainbow PUSH Coalition before winning the open seat vacated by Bobby Rush, and he sits on the House Agriculture and Foreign Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Jackson was born in Chicago in 1966 to civil rights leaders Rev. Jesse Jackson and Jacqueline Jackson, and his official biography says his background is rooted in civil rights activism.

He attended Whitney M. Young Magnet High School in Chicago, then earned a bachelor's degree in business from North Carolina A&T State University in 1988 and an MBA from Northwestern University in 1991.

Jackson worked as an investment analyst and business owner. With his brother Yusef he became an owner of the Anheuser-Busch distributorship River North Sales and Service in Chicago in 1998, and he later operated Cricket Wireless franchise stores.
He has taught finance and entrepreneurship, including at City Colleges of Chicago, and is a business professor at Chicago State University, according to Wikipedia.

As national spokesman for the Rainbow PUSH Coalition, he worked, according to his official biography, on wrongful-conviction cases including those of Darrell Cannon, Oscar Walden and Johnnie Lee Savory.
He also took part in international human rights negotiations, including talks that helped secure the release of Navy Lt. Robert Goodman from Syria and 22 Americans detained in Cuba.
Jackson won the 2022 Democratic primary for the open 1st District seat after Rep. Bobby Rush announced his retirement, and he took office in January 2023.
He won renomination in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating Jerico Brown, and for the 119th Congress he serves on the House Agriculture and Foreign Affairs committees.

sources.title: Christian Maxwell (campaign website text, Feb. 26, 2025, and Candidate Connection survey)
